question.text: An AIF sponsor is comparing the Trust versus the LLP versus the Company route. Which of the following is a genuine downside of using an LLP structure for an AIF in India?

answer.text: An LLP cannot be a taxable entity under the Income-tax Act
An LLP is not permitted to raise capital commitments from foreign investors
An LLP cannot have more than 50 partners as per the LLP Act 2008
LLP investors become partners, and their details come into public domain via MCA filings, losing the secrecy of a trust

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.4 Alternative 2 lists the LLP downside: higher MCA compliance and loss of secrecy since partner details sit in the public domain. The trust route keeps investor identities private. The Trap: Option A is wrong — LLPs are taxable entities. Option C confuses the old 'firm' 20-partner cap — LLPs have no such cap. Option D is false — FDI in LLPs is permitted under automatic route subject to conditions. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B describe LLPs superficially. XIX-C tests the nuanced MCA-disclosure downside which is a real Manager concern. Manager's Pro-Tip: HNI LPs who prize anonymity will reject an LLP AIF outright. If you have privacy-sensitive family offices on your anchor list, stay with the trust structure.
